data.name: AutoLand.AirportListDescription

data.name: Autostart.TakeoffDescription
data.value: After six takeoff approvals: Thrust ramp, centerline guidance, rotation at model VR and stabilized initial climb. Handover to the local AP/ALT/HDG/LVL/thrust controllers once climb above 50 ft AGL and at least model VY are confirmed. Provisional remaining-runway reserve defaults to 200 m; no stopping guarantee. Terrain following and waypoint tracking remain off.

data.name: InfoDialog_Text
data.value:
AutoFly
Version {{VERSION}}
Fly, observe and automate
AutoFly is a companion application for Microsoft Flight Simulator. It connects to the simulator via SimConnect, displays flight data and the aircraft position on a map, and supports automatic flight guidance.
Features include local autopilot control for heading, altitude and speed, waypoint navigation, terrain following, and automatic takeoff and landing procedures. AutoFly is intended for exploring, experimenting with and better understanding automated flights in the simulator. The user remains responsible for monitoring and operation.
For flight simulation only – not for real aircraft or real-world navigation.
And if anyone asks what this is good for: To paraphrase Pomax; simply because we can!
Special thanks to Pomax
My special thanks go to Pomax and his JavaScript application “Are we flying?”. Without his idea and his clear, illustrative work, I would never have come up with AutoFly – and would not have been able to complete this project.
https://pomax.github.io/are-we-flying
Thanks for the support
I would also like to thank GitHub Copilot Chat Agent GPT-6.1-Sol for supporting the development. Without this help, I would not have been able to create AutoFly either.
Freeware: Info to MASUSoftware@kabelmail.de
